Subject: Post-signature implementation slate & canary migration schedule — OpalHealth

Hi Susan —

Great to be officially partnered — congrats to the teams on getting the SOW across the finish line. Per our close conversation, I attached a first-draft implementation slate ("MAP-OpalHealth-v1.xlsx") that embeds the mutual action plan alongside the SOW milestones and a proposed evaluation plan. High level items included: rollout cadence, canary gating criteria, migration windows, training cadence, and acceptance gates.

Quick summary of proposed timeline (please confirm):
- Training kickoff (train-the-trainer): 2028-06-05 to 2028-06-06 (remote, 2 half-days)
- Dry-run / pre-canary smoke: 2028-06-01 (internal dry-run with sample traffic)
- Canary window (limited-production traffic): 2028-06-12 to 2028-06-19
- Migration & cutover target: 2028-06-25 to 2028-06-26 (weekend)
- Post-cutover hypercare: 2028-06-26 to 2028-07-03

Proposed evaluation checkpoints (also in the sheet):
- Performance: p95 generation latency < 150ms on production-like load
- Throughput: baseline target 10 req/s for initial canary pool
- Quality: evaluation set F1 >= 0.78 (we'll publish the eval harness)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% sustained across 24h windows

We flagged a few decision points that need Opal signoff in the MAP:
1) Canary sample size (we proposed 3% of live traffic)
2) Rollback thresholds (we proposed auto-fallback if p95 latency degrades by > 50% or error rate > 1.5%)
3) Data retention & log sharing scope for evals (we noted Opal security questions in the sheet)

Attachments: MAP-OpalHealth-v1.xlsx, SOW-OpalHealth-StatementOfWork-v1.pdf

Next asks: can you confirm whether the training week (6/5–6/6) works for your leads, and whether security wants a separate evidence package before the dry-run? If we get alignment this week we can lock the dry-run and schedule the canary start.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Solutions to scope the dry-run and Ops for the migration runbook after your confirmation.

—Laura

Hi Susan —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I pulled together a short implementation & evaluation addendum to the MAP and a gating matrix below (also attached as "EvalPlan-OpalHealth.pdf"). Key changes and clarifications:

1) Training / dry-run cadence
- We can move the public-facing training to 2028-06-01–06-02 (train-the-trainer on 6/1 AM, SME walkthrough 6/1 PM, follow-up half-day 6/2).
- Dry-run (internal with Opal test tokens) scheduled 2028-06-08 (will simulate 48 hours of typical query mix).

2) Canary scheduling & staffing
- Proposed canary window: 2028-06-15 to 2028-06-22 (start mid-week per your preference).
- Canary sample size: start at 2% traffic, expand to 8% by day 3 if gating thresholds are met.
- Monitoring: Redwood on-call + Opal ops (Mike) to be present for first 48 hours.

3) Acceptance / gating matrix (pass/fail rules)
- Performance: p95 latency increase <= 30% vs baseline and absolute p95 <= 200ms.
- Error rate: sustained < 1% over 1 hour windows; immediate rollback if > 2% for 15 minutes.
- Quality: Eval harness F1 >= 0.75 on the agreed test set. Regression alert if any critical intent drops > 3 points.
- Business KPI: conversion/relevant outcome delta monitored but not a hard gate for first canary.

4) Data & security artifacts
- We will provide: SOC2 control mapping (summary), a redaction plan for tokens, and a 30-day sample retention policy for eval logs. Full artifacts will be shared in a secure Drive folder and via DocuSign for acceptance where needed.

Attachments: EvalPlan-OpalHealth.pdf, MAP-OpalHealth-v1.xlsx (updated). Drive runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xYMapRunbook

Action items for Opal (please):
- Confirm training attendee list and who will be the two train-the-trainer leads.
- Confirm acceptance of the gating matrix above (or propose changes).
- Confirm security contact for artifact exchange (email address we can push docs to).

If we get all confirmations this week we’ll lock dates and send a calendar pack with pre-reads.

—Rishi
